# parallel/src/lib.rs (v2026.9.0) [lines 120-170]

```rust
120:     pub trait Strategy: Clone + Send + Sync + fmt::Debug + 'static {
121:         /// Returns a strategy wrapper for manually partitioned work.
122:         fn manual(&self) -> Manual<Self>
123:         where
124:             Self: Sized;
125: 
126:         /// Submit one CPU-bound job to this strategy, running it inline on the calling task when
127:         /// it is measured cheaper than the round trip of offloading it to the pool.
128:         ///
129:         /// `len` groups calls at a call site into size classes for those measurements, so similar
130:         /// `len` must mean comparable cost. An inline job runs to completion before `spawn`
131:         /// returns, and jobs whose measured cost exceeds a small time budget offload. To force a
132:         /// hand-off on a multi-worker pool, submit through [`manual`](Self::manual).
133:         ///
134:         /// The returned future resolves when the job completes. Blocking on external
135:         /// synchronization or I/O inside the job can occupy execution capacity until it returns.
136:         /// When the polling thread itself belongs to the strategy's execution resources (e.g. a
137:         /// runtime whose executor thread is registered as a pool worker), the job (and other
138:         /// pending work) may be executed inline on that thread rather than waited on.
139:         ///
140:         /// If the job panics, the panic is propagated to the caller; it never aborts the process.
141:         #[track_caller]
142:         fn spawn<F, T>(
143:             &self,
144:             len: usize,
145:             f: F,
146:         ) -> impl core::future::Future<Output = T> + Send + 'static
147:         where
148:             F: FnOnce(Self) -> T + Send + 'static,
149:             T: Send + 'static;
150: 
151:         /// Runs either a serial or parallel body.
152:         #[track_caller]
153:         fn run<R, SEQ, PAR>(&self, len: usize, serial: SEQ, parallel: PAR) -> R
154:         where
155:             R: Send,
156:             SEQ: FnOnce() -> R + Send,
157:             PAR: FnOnce() -> R + Send;
158: 
159:         /// Like [`run`](Self::run), but for fallible work.
160:         ///
161:         /// The strategy chooses and runs either the serial or parallel body, returning the
162:         /// first error produced by the chosen body. Elapsed time is only recorded on success,
163:         /// so abort-early error paths cannot poison the adaptive policy's estimates.
164:         #[track_caller]
165:         fn try_run<R, E, SEQ, PAR>(&self, len: usize, serial: SEQ, parallel: PAR) -> Result<R, E>
166:         where
167:             R: Send,
168:             E: Send,
169:             SEQ: FnOnce() -> Result<R, E> + Send,
170:             PAR: FnOnce() -> Result<R, E> + Send;
```
